title: Boss: build your own Actions runner
summary: Matrix exclusions, cycle detection, parallel waves and job conditions.

steps.title: The scheduler
steps.body: GitHub has to turn your YAML into a plan before a single runner starts: expand matrices, check the `needs` graph and decide which jobs run when. You are writing that planner.

steps.title: Matrix with exclude
prompt: Write `List<string> ExpandWithExclude(List<(string Key, List<string> Values)> axes, List<string> exclude)`.
Expand like before (`"os=ubuntu,dotnet=8"`, last axis fastest). Each exclude entry is a **partial** combination such as `"os=windows"` or
`"os=macos,dotnet=8"`; drop every combination that contains **all** of an entry's `key=value` pairs.
starter: List<string> ExpandWithExclude(List<(string Key, List<string> Values)> axes, List<string> exclude)
solution: List<string> ExpandWithExclude(List<(string Key, List<string> Values)> axes, List<string> exclude)
hints: A combination is excluded when `entry.Split(',').All(pair => combo.Split(',').Contains(pair))`.
template: var dojoAxes = new List<(string Key, List<string> Values)> { ("os", new() { "ubuntu", "windows", "macos" }), ("dotnet", new() { "8", "9" }) };
Dojo.Eq("partial entry drops a whole row", new List<string> { "os=ubuntu,dotnet=8", "os=ubuntu,dotnet=9", "os=macos,dotnet=8", "os=macos,dotnet=9" },
Dojo.Eq("order of pairs in the entry does not matter", 5, ExpandWithExclude(dojoAxes, new() { "dotnet=9,os=ubuntu" }).Count);

steps.title: Reject cycles
prompt: Write `ExecutionOrder` again (ready jobs alphabetically), but now it must throw `InvalidOperationException` when the jobs cannot all run:
a cycle, or a job that needs a job that does not exist.
solution: var waiting = needs.ToDictionary(p => p.Key, p => p.Value.Count);
var ready = new SortedSet<string>(waiting.Where(p => p.Value == 0).Select(p => p.Key), StringComparer.Ordinal);
if (order.Count < needs.Count) throw new InvalidOperationException("needs contains a cycle or an unknown job");
hints: If the loop ends with fewer jobs in the order than there are jobs, something could never become ready.
A job needing a missing job never reaches zero waiting dependencies, so the same check catches it.

steps.title: Parallel waves
prompt: Runners execute every ready job at once. Write `List<string> Waves(Dictionary<string, List<string>> needs)` that returns each wave of
jobs that start together, as an alphabetical comma-joined string. Throw `InvalidOperationException` if the graph cannot finish.
hints: A job is in the next wave when it is not done and all of its needs are done.
If a round finds no such job but work remains, the graph is stuck.

steps.title: Job conditions
prompt: Write `bool ShouldRun(string condition, List<string> needResults)` where each result is `"success"`, `"failure"` or `"skipped"`:
Any other condition throws `ArgumentException`. With no needs, `success()` runs and `failure()` does not.
solution: bool ShouldRun(string condition, List<string> needResults) => condition switch
hints: A `switch` expression over the condition string fits well.
`All` on an empty list is true and `Any` is false, which is exactly the rule.
template: Dojo.Eq("success() with all green", true, ShouldRun("success()", new() { "success", "success" }));
Dojo.Eq("success() with a skipped need", false, ShouldRun("success()", new() { "success", "skipped" }));
Dojo.Eq("failure() notifies on failure", true, ShouldRun("failure()", new() { "success", "failure" }));
Dojo.Eq("failure() stays quiet when green", false, ShouldRun("failure()", new() { "success" }));
Dojo.Eq("always() cleans up", true, ShouldRun("always()", new() { "failure" }));
Dojo.Eq("no needs: success() runs", true, ShouldRun("success()", new()));
